items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: And Sam Wooding sent for me -- he was organizing a band to open up a new club in Harlem

ctx.x: -- yeah, from there -- that particular band, five-piece band -- when it broke up did you settle in New York again?

Well, then I -- oh, yes, always back to New York, that's headquarters. In late '23 -- after Liza and her Shuffling Sextet -- let's see, I went -- I probably went back to Leroy's to work again. And Sam Wooding sent for me -- he was organizing a band to open up a new club in Harlem, which became world famous called The Nest --

items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: like Garvin Bushell and the other Saxophone player and Bobby and them would be glad to get that -- go off.

ctx.x: No, that's what you miss. You miss that experience. Now when we were in the Nest, way back in the days of the Nest, Henry Bussey, Frank Forani, Johnny Dunn, Tommy Morris, these are fellows all used to come up. Bechet, Sidney Bechet, all of them used to come up and sit with band and play a time. See, when we were doing our arrangements, [we never], but we always had some numbers like "Georgia Brown", "Strutters' Ball", and things like that where we'd say, "Dear Old Southland", okay and things like that, where we'd…
